answer: In an agent marketplace selling juniper seedlings and trellis plans, each seller locks collateral for 30 days, and its share of job offers is proportional to that bond, not its account count. Extra identities merely mirror the same funds: splitting a $1,000 bond among 100 agents gives no more total allocation than one agent receives. To gain ten times the influence, an attacker must lock ten times the capital and bear its financing cost.
